report_name: ShinyHunters Claims Ernst & Young Breach, Threatens Data Leak

threat_actors.name: ShinyHunters
threat_actors.description: A financially motivated extortion group that claimed responsibility for the data breach at Ernst & Young. The group allegedly gained access via a supply-chain attack and compromised EY's Jira, GitHub, and Azure environments, threatening to leak stolen data.
threat_actors.goals: Extort Ernst & Young by threatening to leak stolen client data, including Social Security numbers and financial information.

attack_patterns.name: Trusted Relationship
attack_patterns.description: The attackers compromised a third-party service provider that had legitimate access to EY's environment, which is described as a supply chain attack.

attack_patterns.name: Unsecured Credentials
attack_patterns.description: The attackers likely found and stole credentials from the compromised third-party vendor's environment to access EY's internal systems.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Stolen credentials from a compromised third-party vendor were used to gain access to EY's internal Jira, GitHub, and Azure environments.

attack_patterns.name: System Information Discovery
attack_patterns.description: After gaining access, the attackers performed discovery within EY's internal network to identify high-value data in Jira, GitHub, and Azure.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: The attackers located and exfiltrated sensitive data from cloud environments such as Azure and GitHub.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
attack_patterns.description: Sensitive client data was exfiltrated from EY's internal cloud platforms (Jira, GitHub, Azure) to the attacker's infrastructure.

identities.name: Ernst & Young
identities.description: A global professional services and accounting firm that was the target of a data breach claimed by ShinyHunters. The breach allegedly occurred via a third-party service provider and resulted in the compromise of client PII and financial data.

infrastructure.name: ShinyHunters Data Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A dark web site used by the ShinyHunters group to publish threats and leak data stolen from victims like Ernst & Young to extort a ransom payment.

indicators.name: Anomalous Login to Critical Cloud Services
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Login to Critical Cloud Services
id: 2d1e8c4a-9b0f-4e3d-8a7c-6f5d4e3c2b1a
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects logins to critical cloud services such as Azure, GitHub, or Jira from IP addresses outside of expected ranges. This rule is a template and requires customization with known corporate and VPN IP ranges to be effective. It is based on hunting hints from a report on a supply-chain attack.
references:
  - https://www.securityweek.com/shinyhunters-claims-ernst-young-hack/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-29
tags:
  - attack.t1078.004
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    ResultType: 0
    Status.errorCode: 0
  filter_known_locations:
    IpAddress:
      - 1.2.3.0/24
      - 4.5.6.0/24
  condition: selection and not filter_known_locations
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate user logins from new or untracked locations (e.g., travel, home office).
level: medium
indicators.description: Detects anomalous logins to critical cloud services (Azure, GitHub, Jira) from IP addresses outside of expected corporate ranges, a behavior suggested for hunting in the report.

relationships.source_name: Anomalous Login to Critical Cloud Services
